Add a hockey rink to a ggplot

Source: R/annotate_rink.R
annotate_rink.Rd

Draws the rink markings and sets up the plot canvas in one call: the rink layers, a coordinate system for the chosen orientation and, unless theme = FALSE, theme_rink(). Add it right after ggplot(), before your geoms, and map your data in regular horizontal rink coordinates (x along the length, y across the width, in the frame of dimensions). For orientation = "vertical" the display is rotated for you, so the same data works in either orientation.

Usage

annotate_rink(
  colour = "#143F84",
  fill = "#eaf2f8",
  dimensions = IIHF,
  orientation = c("horizontal", "vertical"),
  zones = c("dz", "nz", "oz"),
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  margin = 0.5,
  zone_margin = 2,
  linewidth = 0.3,
  details = FALSE,
  slot = FALSE,
  slot_colour = "grey",
  slot_fill = NA,
  slot_alpha = 0.7,
  slot_linewidth = 0.4,
  logos = NULL,
  logo_alpha = 0.25,
  theme = TRUE
)

Arguments

colour

Colour of the rink markings.

fill

Colour of the ice.

dimensions

Rink dimensions to draw, e.g. IIHF (default) or NHL; see rink_dims and rink_dimensions().

orientation

"horizontal" (default) or "vertical" (the right-hand end, the offensive zone, at the top).

zones

Which zones to show, a subset of c("dz", "nz", "oz") (default all three); "oz" is the high-x end. Sets xlim for you, e.g. c("dz", "nz") crops to the defensive and neutral zones. Ignored if xlim is given.

xlim, ylim

Optional plot limits in rink coordinates, to crop by hand. xlim overrides zones; ylim defaults to the full width plus margin.

margin

Space (in rink units) added beyond the end and side boards.

zone_margin

Space added beyond a blue line when zones stops there, so the crop runs a little past the line instead of ending on it.

linewidth

Multiplier for the rink line widths (lines_small / lines_big in dimensions). ggplot2 line widths are absolute (mm on the page), so they don't shrink with the plot: the default 0.3 suits a rink a few inches across; go lower (e.g. 0.2) for small or heavily faceted rinks and higher (e.g. 0.6-1) for a large poster-size rink.

details

If TRUE, draw the faceoff hash marks and the dot cut-outs.

slot

If TRUE, shade the offensive-zone slot.

slot_colour, slot_fill, slot_alpha, slot_linewidth

Slot styling.

logos

Optional logos to place on the ice, as a named list with any of centre, left and right (centre ice, and just inside each blue line). Each entry is a path to a PNG file or an image already in memory (an array as returned by png::readPNG(), a matrix of colours or a raster). Reading PNG files needs the png package. No logos ship with gghockey: bring the ones you have the rights to use.

logo_alpha

Opacity of the logos, between 0 and 1.

theme

If TRUE (default), add theme_rink() (and, for vertical rinks, the matching aspect ratio). Set FALSE to supply your own theme.

Value

A list of ggplot2 components (rink layers, a coordinate system and, optionally, a theme) to add to a plot.

See also

rink_geometry() for the markings as data, geom_rink_bin() for heatmaps on the rink.

Examples

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(shots, aes(x, y)) +
  annotate_rink() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3)


# Vertical, offensive zone only, with hash marks:
ggplot(shots, aes(x, y)) +
  annotate_rink(orientation = "vertical", zones = "oz", details = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = factor(goal)), alpha = 0.5)


# NHL rink, in the colours of your choice:
ggplot() +
  annotate_rink(dimensions = NHL, colour = "grey30", fill = "white")
